tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application. Finder is an application like any other: clicking the desktop, the Dock, or a Finder window (including Go to Folder) requires a Finder grant. The menu bar does not, as long as the app that is frontmost is one you already have access to.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

"""Independent reference implementation of the commission spec (spec.md only).

Written from FR-005..FR-018 + Clarifications. Deliberately NOT derived from the engine.
"""
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_DOWN, getcontext
from datetime import date
import calendar

getcontext().prec = 60

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def r2(x):
    """FR-018: round to the cent, half away from zero."""
    return Decimal(x).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def d(s):
    y, m, dd = (int(p) for p in s.split("-"))
    return date(y, m, dd)


def days_inclusive(a, b):
    return (b - a).days + 1


def split_shares(amount, splits):
    """FR-012 largest remainder. splits: list of (repId, pct as Decimal).

    Returns list of Decimal shares aligned with splits.
    """
    n = len(splits)
    raw = [amount * pct / Decimal(100) for _, pct in splits]
    floors = [x.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_DOWN) for x in raw]
    rems = [raw[i] - floors[i] for i in range(n)]
    leftover = int(((amount - sum(floors)) / CENT).to_integral_value())
    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (-rems[i], i))
    for k in range(leftover):
        floors[order[k % n]] += CENT
    return floors


def tier_lines(bookings, quota):
    """FR-006/FR-007/FR-018. Returns (total, [(label, slice, amount)])."""
    lines = []
    b1 = min(bookings, quota)
    if b1 > 0:
        lines.append(("5%", b1, r2(b1 * Decimal("0.05"))))
    edge = r2(quota * Decimal("1.5"))  # FR-018 lists "the 150% band edge" as rounded
    if bookings > quota:
        b2 = min(bookings, edge) - quota
        if b2 > 0:
            lines.append(("8%", b2, r2(b2 * Decimal("0.08"))))
    if bookings > edge:
        b3 = bookings - edge
        if b3 > 0:
            lines.append(("12%", b3, r2(b3 * Decimal("0.12"))))
    return sum((a for _, _, a in lines), Decimal(0)), lines


def prorated_quota(quota, start, q_start, q_end):
    """FR-010."""
    if start <= q_start:
        return quota
    days = days_inclusive(start, q_end)
    total = days_inclusive(q_start, q_end)
    return r2(quota * Decimal(days) / Decimal(total))


def months_of(q_start, q_end):
    out = []
    y, m = q_start.year, q_start.month
    while True:
        last = date(y, m, calendar.monthrange(y, m)[1])
        out.append((date(y, m, 1), last))
        if last >= q_end:
            break
        m += 1
        if m == 13:
            m, y = 1, y + 1
    return out


def draw_lines(start, q_start, q_end):
    """FR-014."""
    out = []
    for first, last in months_of(q_start, q_end):
        dim = days_inclusive(first, last)
        if start <= first:
            amt = Decimal("4000.00")
        elif start <= last:
            amt = r2(Decimal(4000) * Decimal(days_inclusive(start, last)) / Decimal(dim))
        else:
            amt = Decimal("0.00")
        out.append((first, amt))
    return out


class QuarterCtx:
    """One quarter a rep may have commission computed for (this quarter or a booking quarter)."""

    def __init__(self, key, q_start, q_end, quota, start, deals):
        self.key = key
        self.q_start = q_start
        self.q_end = q_end
        self.quota = quota
        self.start = start
        self.deals = deals  # list of deal dicts, in listed order
        self.pq = prorated_quota(quota, start, q_start, q_end)

    def rep_credit(self, rep_id, applied):
        """Credited bookings for rep with `applied` = {(deal_idx, refund_idx)} applied."""
        total = Decimal(0)
        for di, deal in enumerate(self.deals):
            if not any(s[0] == rep_id for s in deal["splits"]):
                continue
            bk = d(deal["book"])
            if not (self.q_start <= bk <= self.q_end):
                continue
            reduced = Decimal(deal["amount"])
            for ri, rf in enumerate(deal["refunds"]):
                if (di, ri) in applied:
                    reduced -= Decimal(rf[0])
            shares = split_shares(reduced, [(s[0], Decimal(s[1])) for s in deal["splits"]])
            for i, s in enumerate(deal["splits"]):
                if s[0] == rep_id:
                    total += shares[i]
        return total

    def rep_share_of_deal(self, rep_id, di, applied):
        deal = self.deals[di]
        reduced = Decimal(deal["amount"])
        for ri, rf in enumerate(deal["refunds"]):
            if (di, ri) in applied:
                reduced -= Decimal(rf[0])
        shares = split_shares(reduced, [(s[0], Decimal(s[1])) for s in deal["splits"]])
        for i, s in enumerate(deal["splits"]):
            if s[0] == rep_id:
                return reduced, shares[i]
        return reduced, None

    def commission(self, rep_id, applied):
        total, _ = tier_lines(self.rep_credit(rep_id, applied), self.pq)
        return total


def compute(scenario):

    roster = {r["repId"]: r for r in scenario["roster"]}
    statements = []

    for rep in scenario["roster"]:
        rid = rep["repId"]
        quota = Decimal(rep["quota"])
        start = d(rep["start"])
        opening = Decimal(rep.get("opening", "0"))
        pq = prorated_quota(quota, start, q_start, q_end)

        lines = []
        lines.append(("FR-005", quota, "Quarterly quota"))
        if pq != quota:
            lines.append(("FR-010", pq,
                          f"Prorated quota ({days_inclusive(start, q_end)} of {days_inclusive(q_start, q_end)} days)"))

        # credit / excluded lines
        bookings = Decimal(0)
        for deal in scenario["deals"]:
            if not any(s[0] == rid for s in deal["splits"]):
                continue
            bk = d(deal["book"])
            if q_start <= bk <= q_end:
                shares = split_shares(Decimal(deal["amount"]),
                                      [(s[0], Decimal(s[1])) for s in deal["splits"]])
                sh = sum(shares[i] for i, s in enumerate(deal["splits"]) if s[0] == rid)
                bookings += sh
                fr = "FR-012" if len(deal["splits"]) > 1 else "FR-008"
                lines.append((fr, sh, f"{deal['dealId']} credit"))
            else:
                lines.append(("FR-008", Decimal("0.00"), f"{deal['dealId']} excluded"))
        lines.append(("FR-008", bookings, "Credited bookings"))

        before, tls = tier_lines(bookings, pq)
        for label, sl, amt in tls:
            lines.append(("FR-006", amt, f"{label} of {sl}"))
        lines.append(("FR-006", before, "Commission before refunds"))

        # ---- quarter contexts for clawbacks ----
        ctxs = []
        own_deals = [dl for dl in scenario["deals"] if q_start <= d(dl["book"]) <= q_end]
        ctxs.append(QuarterCtx("own", q_start, q_end, quota, start, own_deals))
        for bq in scenario.get("bookingQuarters", []):
            entry = next((r for r in bq["reps"] if r["repId"] == rid), None)
            if entry is None:
                continue
            ctxs.append(QuarterCtx(bq["quarter"][0], d(bq["quarter"][0]), d(bq["quarter"][1]),
                                   Decimal(entry["quota"]), d(entry["start"]), bq["deals"]))

        claw_events = []
        for ctx in ctxs:
            # all refunds on deals in this quarter credited to this rep, any date
            evs = []
            for di, deal in enumerate(ctx.deals):
                if not any(s[0] == rid for s in deal["splits"]):
                    continue
                if not (ctx.q_start <= d(deal["book"]) <= ctx.q_end):
                    continue
                for ri, rf in enumerate(deal["refunds"]):
                    evs.append((d(rf[1]), di, ri, deal, Decimal(rf[0])))
            evs.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0], e[1], e[2]))
            applied = set()
            prev = ctx.commission(rid, applied)
            for (rdate, di, ri, deal, ramt) in evs:
                applied = applied | {(di, ri)}
                cur = ctx.commission(rid, applied)
                claw = prev - cur
                if q_start <= rdate <= q_end:
                    resplit = None
                    if len(deal["splits"]) > 1:
                        reduced, sh = ctx.rep_share_of_deal(rid, di, applied)
                        resplit = (reduced, sh)
                    claw_events.append((rdate, di, ri, deal, ramt, claw, resplit))
                prev = cur

        claw_events.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0], e[1], e[2]))
        total_claw = Decimal(0)
        for (rdate, di, ri, deal, ramt, claw, resplit) in claw_events:
            if resplit is not None:
                lines.append(("FR-017", resplit[1],
                              f"{deal['dealId']} re-split after refund on {rdate}: share of {resplit[0]}"))
            lines.append(("FR-016", claw,
                          f"Clawback: {deal['dealId']} refund {ramt} on {rdate}"))
            total_claw += claw
        lines.append(("FR-016", total_claw, "Clawbacks"))

        earned = before - total_claw
        lines.append(("FR-015", earned, "Earned commission"))

        dls = draw_lines(start, q_start, q_end)
        draws = Decimal(0)
        for first, amt in dls:
            lines.append(("FR-014", amt, f"Draw, {first.strftime('%B %Y')}"))
            draws += amt
        lines.append(("FR-014", draws, "Draws paid"))

        recoverable = opening + draws
        if earned >= 0:
            recovered = min(earned, recoverable)
            payable = earned - recovered
            closing = recoverable - recovered
        else:
            recovered = Decimal("0.00")
            payable = Decimal("0.00")
            closing = recoverable + (-earned)

        lines.append(("FR-015", opening, "Opening recoverable balance"))
        lines.append(("FR-015", recovered, "Draw recovered"))
        lines.append(("FR-015", payable, "Commission payable"))
        lines.append(("FR-015", closing, "Closing recoverable balance"))

        statements.append({
            "repId": rid,
            "quota": quota,
            "proratedQuota": pq,
            "creditedBookings": bookings,
            "commissionBeforeRefunds": before,
            "clawbacks": total_claw,
            "earned": earned,
            "drawPaid": draws,
            "recovered": recovered,
            "payable": payable,
            "closing": closing,
            "lines": lines,
        })

    return statements

            lines.append(("FR-016", claw,

        earned = before - total_claw
        lines.append(("FR-015", earned, "Earned commission"))

        dls = draw_lines(start, q_start, q_end)
        draws = Decimal(0)
        for first, amt in dls:
            lines.append(("FR-014", amt, f"Draw, {first.strftime('%B %Y')}"))
            draws += amt
        lines.append(("FR-014", draws, "Draws paid"))

        if earned >= 0:
            recovered = min(earned, recoverable)
            payable = earned - recovered
            closing = recoverable - recovered
        else:
            recovered = Decimal("0.00")
            payable = Decimal("0.00")
            closing = recoverable + (-earned)

        lines.append(("FR-015", recovered, "Draw recovered"))
        lines.append(("FR-015", payable, "Commission payable"))
        lines.append(("FR-015", closing, "Closing recoverable balance"))

            "proratedQuota": pq,

            "commissionBeforeRefunds": before,
            "clawbacks": total_claw,
            "earned": earned,
            "drawPaid": draws,
            "recovered": recovered,
            "payable": payable,
            "closing": closing,
            "lines": lines,
        })

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from decimal import Decimal
from reference import compute

HERE = "<scratch>/scratchpad/adversarial"

SCALARS = ["quota", "proratedQuota", "creditedBookings", "commissionBeforeRefunds",
           "clawbacks", "earned", "drawPaid", "recovered", "payable", "closing"]


def run_engine(scenarios, tag):
    inp = f"{HERE}/{tag}.in.json"
    out = f"{HERE}/{tag}.out.json"
    with open(inp, "w") as f:
        json.dump(scenarios, f)
    p = subprocess.run(["dotnet", "run", "--project", f"{HERE}/adv.csproj", "--", inp, out],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=HERE)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        print(p.stdout, p.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    return json.load(open(out))


def main(tag):
    scenarios = json.load(open(f"{HERE}/{tag}.scenarios.json"))
    results = run_engine(scenarios, tag)
    by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in results}
    for sc in scenarios:
        r = by_id[sc["id"]]
        note = sc.get("note", "")
        header = f"=== {sc['id']}  {note}"
        expect_reject = sc.get("expectReject", False)
        if r["status"] != "ok":
            print(header)
            print(f"  ENGINE {r['status']}: {r.get('errors') or r.get('exception')}")
            if not expect_reject:
                print("  !! expected a calculation")
            print()
            continue
        if expect_reject:
            print(header)
            print("  !! ENGINE ACCEPTED but scenario should be rejected")
        try:
            ref = compute(sc)
        except Exception as e:
            print(header)
            print(f"  reference threw: {e!r}")
            print()
            continue
        diffs = []
        for eng_st, ref_st in zip(r["statements"], ref):
            assert eng_st["repId"] == ref_st["repId"], (eng_st["repId"], ref_st["repId"])
            for k in SCALARS:
                a, b = Decimal(eng_st[k]), Decimal(ref_st[k])
                if a != b:
                    diffs.append(f"  {eng_st['repId']}.{k}: engine={a} ref={b}  delta={a-b}")
            el = [(l["fr"], Decimal(l["amount"])) for l in eng_st["lines"]]
            rl = [(fr, amt) for fr, amt, _ in ref_st["lines"]]
            if el != rl:
                diffs.append(f"  {eng_st['repId']}: LINE SEQUENCE differs")
                for i in range(max(len(el), len(rl))):
                    e = el[i] if i < len(el) else None
                    rr = rl[i] if i < len(rl) else None
                    mark = "   " if e == rr else " * "
                    ed = eng_st["lines"][i]["desc"] if i < len(el) else ""
                    rd = ref_st["lines"][i][2] if i < len(rl) else ""
                    diffs.append(f"   {mark}{i:2d} eng={e} [{ed}]   ref={rr} [{rd}]")
        if diffs or expect_reject:
            print(header)
            print("\n".join(diffs))
            print()
        else:
            print(f"{header}  -> MATCH")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1])

"""Boundary-biased fuzz: bookings placed a cent either side of the 100% and 150% edges,
often with an odd prorated quota, and refunds sized to land exactly on an edge."""
import json
import random
import sys
from datetime import date, timedelta
from decimal import Decimal

sys.path.insert(0, "<scratch>/scratchpad/adversarial")
from reference import prorated_quota, r2  # only to place bookings near an edge, not to predict output

HERE = "<scratch>/scratchpad/adversarial"

QUARTERS = [
    (date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 3, 31)),
    (date(2026, 4, 1), date(2026, 6, 30)),
    (date(2026, 7, 1), date(2026, 9, 30)),
    (date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 3, 31)),
    (date(2026, 10, 1), date(2026, 12, 31)),
]


def make(rng, idx):
    qs, qe = rng.choice(QUARTERS)
    quota_c = rng.randint(1_00, 500_000_00)
    quota = Decimal(quota_c) / 100
    mid = rng.random() < 0.6
    start = qs + timedelta(days=rng.randint(1, (qe - qs).days)) if mid else qs - timedelta(days=30)
    pq = prorated_quota(quota, start, qs, qe)
    if pq <= 0:
        return None

    target_base = rng.choice([pq, r2(pq * Decimal("1.5")), pq * Decimal("1.5")])
    delta = Decimal(rng.randint(-3, 3)) / 100
    target = (target_base + delta).quantize(Decimal("0.01"))
    if target <= 0:
        target = Decimal("0.01")

    # split the target across 1-3 deals, all credited 100% to the rep
    n = rng.randint(1, 3)
    cents = int(target * 100)
    cuts = sorted(rng.sample(range(1, max(2, cents)), min(n - 1, max(0, cents - 1)))) if cents > 1 else []
    parts, prev = [], 0
    for c in cuts + [cents]:
        parts.append(c - prev)
        prev = c
    parts = [p for p in parts if p > 0] or [cents]

    deals = []
    for k, p in enumerate(parts):
        book = max(start, qs) + timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, (qe - max(start, qs)).days))
        refunds = []
        if rng.random() < 0.45 and p > 1:
            r = rng.randint(1, p - 1)
            refunds.append([f"{r / 100:.2f}", (book + timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 120))).isoformat()])
        deals.append({"dealId": f"D{k}", "amount": f"{p / 100:.2f}",
                      "close": book.isoformat(), "book": book.isoformat(),
                      "splits": [["r0", "100"]], "refunds": refunds})

    return {"id": f"g{idx}", "note": "", "quarter": [qs.isoformat(), qe.isoformat()],
            "roster": [{"repId": "r0", "quota": f"{quota_c / 100:.2f}", "start": start.isoformat(),
                        "opening": "0" if rng.random() < 0.6 else f"{rng.randint(0, 2_000_00) / 100:.2f}"}],
            "deals": deals, "bookingQuarters": []}


def main(seed, n):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = []
    i = 0
    while len(out) < n:
        s = make(rng, i)
        i += 1
        if s:
            out.append(s)
    with open(f"{HERE}/fuzz.scenarios.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=1)
    print("ok", len(out))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]))

I audited the engine as a black box against the spec, using an independently written reference implementation (Python, from FR-005–FR-018 + Clarifications only) plus ~4,950 differential scenarios.

## Findings

### 1. An earlier-quarter deal listed in both the scenario's deal list and booking-quarter data is always falsely rejected — entire statement suppressed

**Input** (JSON as fed to `CommissionEngine.Calculate`; the two `E1` entries are byte-for-byte identical):

```json
{"id":"dup","quarter":["2026-04-01","2026-06-30"],

   {"dealId":"Q2D","amount":"40000.00","close":"2026-05-01","book":"2026-05-04","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[]},
   {"dealId":"E1","amount":"60000.00","close":"2026-01-09","book":"2026-01-10","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[["60000.00","2026-04-15"]]}],
 "bookingQuarters":[{"quarter":["2026-01-01","2026-03-31"],
   "reps":[{"repId":"r1","quota":"100000.00","start":"2025-06-01"}],"partners":[],
   "deals":[
     {"dealId":"E1","amount":"60000.00","close":"2026-01-09","book":"2026-01-10","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[["60000.00","2026-04-15"]]},
     {"dealId":"E2","amount":"60000.00","close":"2026-02-09","book":"2026-02-10","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[]}]}]}
```

**Spec contradicted** — FR-004 rejects only when they *differ*: "or an earlier-quarter deal listed both in the scenario's own deal list and in booking-quarter data **differs between the two**". Here they do not differ. FR-004 also requires a rejected scenario to "MUST NOT show any payout", so a false rejection suppresses the whole statement.

**Expected** (derived twice; the second derivation is Appendix A.10 Sage, which is the identical shape): Q1 commission before refunds = 5% × $100,000.00 = $5,000.00 plus 8% × $20,000.00 = $1,600.00 → $6,600.00; with E1 removed, bookings $60,000.00 → 5% = $3,000.00; clawback = $6,600.00 − $3,000.00 = **$3,600.00**. Q2: credited bookings $40,000.00, 5% = $2,000.00; earned = $2,000.00 − $3,600.00 = **−$1,600.00**; draws $12,000.00; recovered $0.00; payable $0.00; closing recoverable balance **$13,600.00**. Plus an excluded-deal line for E1 at $0.00 (FR-008).

**Actual**: `RejectedScenario` — `[FR-004] "Deal 'E1' differs between the two lists."` No statement, no payout.

**Root cause, established black-box**: I passed the *same* `DealInput` object instance into both lists → accepted, and the engine then produced exactly the expected statement above. Structurally identical but separately constructed instances → rejected. Sharing only `Splits` → still rejected; only `Refunds` → still rejected; sharing both → accepted. That is C# positional-record equality, whose `IReadOnlyList<SplitCredit>`/`IReadOnlyList<RefundInput>` members compare by *reference*. Any real loader (JSON, file, DB) constructs separate lists, so the check can never pass.

It also fires on refund-free duplicates: adding the identical `E2` to the scenario's own deal list yields two errors, `"Deal 'E1' differs…"` and `"Deal 'E2' differs…"`. This matters because FR-004's precondition requires booking-quarter data to include *every* deal the rep booked that quarter, while the app also lists earlier-quarter deals as excluded (Appendix A.2 B-4) — so the overlap is the natural data shape.

**Dollar impact**: the full statement (here a $3,600.00 clawback and a $13,600.00 closing balance); unbounded in general. **Confidence: high.**

### 2. Spurious rejection reason: "refunds total more than the deal amount" on a deal with no refunds

**Input**: `{"dealId":"X","amount":"-100.00","close":"2026-01-05","book":"2026-01-06","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[]}` in a Q1-2026 scenario.

**Spec contradicted** — FR-004: "A scenario that violates a validation rule … MUST be shown as rejected **with the reasons**"; the rule cited is the Edge Case "A refund of zero or less, or refunds on one deal totalling more than the deal amount, are rejected." There are no refunds; their total is $0.00.

**Expected**: one error — `"Deal 'X': amount must be greater than zero."`
**Actual**: that error **plus** `[FR-004] "Deal 'X': refunds total more than the deal amount."` The guard is evidently `sum(refunds) > amount`, and `0 > −100` is true.

Positive control: a deal of `"0.00"` with no refunds produces only the amount error, so the message is emitted exactly when the amount is negative.

**Dollar impact: $0.00** (the scenario is correctly rejected either way) — it is a wrong reason, not a wrong payout. **Confidence: high.**

## Areas probed hard with no finding

All of the following were checked against the reference to the cent, line for line, including FR IDs and line ordering. Every one is clean.

- **Appendix A**, all 10 calculated scenarios and the rejected one — exact match (this is the positive control for both the engine and my reference).
- **Tier boundaries**: bookings at exactly 100%, 100% ± $0.01, exactly 150%, 150% ± $0.01; quotas with odd cents so the 150% edge lands on a half-cent; quotas of $0.01/$0.03 against $500,000 bookings; half-cent tier-line rounding at 5%, 8%, 12%; zero bookings (no tier lines).
- **The rounded 150% band edge** (FR-018) is genuinely exercised: I searched for inputs where the rounded-edge and unrounded-edge readings differ by a cent, found 2,720 in a small sweep, and ran five realistic ones (e.g. quota $17,394.27, bookings $26,092.95 → $1,565.66 rounded-edge vs $1,565.67 unrounded). The engine follows the rounded edge, as FR-018 explicitly requires.
- **Proration**: start on the quarter's first day, second day, last day; start dates producing half-cent prorated quotas; prorated quota rounding to $0.00 (correctly rejected) and to $0.01; a mid-quarter starter whose prorated quota rounds back to the full quota (the FR-010 line is still emitted — correct).
- **Quarter shapes**: 89/90/91/92-day quarters, leap Q1 2024, a quarter ending on 2024-02-29, and non-calendar-aligned quarters (2025-11-01..2026-01-31, 2026-02-01..2026-04-30).
- **Draws**: start on a month's last day, on a month's first day, on the quarter's last day, on 2024-02-29; half-cent draw rounding.
- **Splits**: $0.01 split 50/50 (tie → first-listed rep) and reversed; 99/1 and 1/99; three-way thirds; seven-way 24-decimal percentages; a four-way tie for two leftover cents; $999,999.99 at 70/30.
- **Refunds**: full, repeated partial, partials totalling exactly the deal; two deals refunded on the same date (and with the deal list reversed); two refunds on one deal on the same date; refunds on the quarter's first and last day and the day after; a refund crossing a tier boundary; one-cent and sub-half-cent refunds; negative clawbacks from re-splits; re-split lines present for split deals and absent for solo deals and for out-of-quarter refunds.
- **Earlier-quarter refunds**: prorated booking-quarter quota; booking-quarter quota differing from this quarter's; two booking quarters in one statement; off-roster split partners participating in the re-split; earlier refunds dated inside the booking quarter applied before sizing the current one; refunds listed out of date order; cross-deal ordering by refund date.
- **Draw recovery**: earned above/below/equal to the recoverable total; opening balances including $0.01; earned exactly $0.00; negative earned with and without an opening balance.
- **Validation**: 43 targeted probes — duplicate repId/dealId (roster, own list, booking-quarter list), rep twice on one deal, empty roster, 0%/>100%/negative split percentages, sums of 99.99%/100.01%, zero/negative/non-cent quotas, deal amounts, refunds and opening balances, refund before booking date, refunds exceeding (and exactly equalling) the deal, quarters of 2/4 months, not starting on the 1st, reversed, one day short, off-roster credit on counted *and* excluded deals, start after quarter end, start on the last day, deal booked before/on a rep's start date (counted and excluded), missing booking-quarter data, overlapping booking quarter, booking quarter not three months, booking-quarter deal booked outside its own dates, booking-quarter start date differing from the roster, missing booking-quarter rep entry, partner with no start date, FR-011 against a partner, and a multi-error scenario. All behaved as the spec requires (aside from finding 2).
- **Randomised differential fuzzing**: 2,800 general scenarios (7 seeds) plus 2,000 boundary-biased scenarios (4 seeds) placing bookings a cent either side of the 100% and 150% edges over odd prorated quotas — **zero** numeric mismatches.

One non-finding worth knowing: `RepStatement.Attainment` is the raw ratio (`0.8`, `1.1111…`), not the two-decimal-place percentage FR-002 describes. FR-002 says attainment "is shown as" a percentage and "is display only", so the formatting belongs to the caller — but the engine's public API gives no rounded value, so a UI that prints it directly would violate FR-002.

## Genuine spec ambiguities

**I found none where two readings pay different amounts.** The clarifications close every payout-affecting question I probed — notably the marginal tiers, booking-date crediting, share-only attainment, calendar-day proration, recompute-based clawbacks, largest-remainder splits with ties to the first-listed rep, re-split after each refund, and FR-018's explicit rounding of the 150% band edge.

Two things are genuinely unspecified but carry a **$0.00 differential**:

1. **Order of clawback lines across booking quarters.** FR-017 fixes the order only within one quarter: "For each rep, all refunds on deals booked in **the same quarter** are applied in refund-date order across deals". When a rep has refunds from this quarter *and* an earlier one (or from two earlier ones), the spec does not say how the lines interleave. The engine groups by quarter (own quarter first, then booking quarters in listed order); a global refund-date order is an equally valid reading. Each clawback is recomputed inside its own quarter, so no amount changes — differential **$0.00**. My reference initially used the date-ordered reading and produced 34 line-order diffs across 400 fuzz cases with every amount identical.

2. **Whether a re-split line is shown for a refund dated outside the scenario's quarter.** The 2026-09-21 analyze clarification says "after each refund on a split deal, the rep's statement shows a line with their re-split share", while FR-016 says "A refund dated after the scenario's quarter ends has no effect on that quarter's statement". The engine shows the re-split line only alongside an in-quarter clawback, consistent with Appendix A.9. Presentation only — differential **$0.00**.
